text:
zoe: quick flag from intake  we've got a backlog where full bench + comp checks are delaying deploys by multiple hours. proposal: a 'rapid-accept' path that uses a tiny "delta-prober" to let safe models into canary faster.

rahul: +1 from infra. want details on what "safe" means. what exact checks run in delta-prober?

zoe: plan sketch: 1) artifact -> compute op-hash manifest 2) run delta-prober (30-90s): op-diff based microbench + 20 golden seeds + a few tail microtraces 3) compatibility smoke: deterministic output checks on a small slice 4) if pass, mark model "provisionally-accepted" and schedule full bench within N hours.

maria: how do we avoid silent perf regressions from quantization packing or kernel reorder? op-diff alone won't catch that.

devon: delta-prober needs two signals: op-hash unchanged AND microtrace perf within threshold. microtrace should include both short and long seqlen, attention-swell, and a small KV-cache warmup run.

rahul: what thresholds? suggest relative thresholds vs baseline (model family head). e.g., 10% p95 increase or 15% average token cost -> fail. Also cap absolute runtime to keep it fast.

kyle: operational tiers matter. we can let "internal/team" models use rapid-accept; customers need opt-in or SLA-based tiers. otherwise we create huge full-bench debt.

zoe: agree on tiers: internal, quick (provisional + full bench in 12h), gated (block until full). default to quick unless customer opts into strict.

maria: need an emergency rollback plan if full bench later fails. automation idea: model registry holds current-serving-variant and last-known-good. if full bench fails, queue auto-roll and emit high-priority alert.

rahul: + add a console indicator "provisional" with TTL and link to pending bench job. helpful for SRE and customers. also expose a metric: delta-prober_passrate and delta-prober_latency.

devon: CLI prototype snippet for delta-prober:
```
delta-prober run \n  --model /artifacts/m-abc123 \n  --ops-manifest /artifacts/m-abc123/ops.json \n  --goldens /golden-sets/optima-family/ \n  --microtraces micro.json \n  --n-seeds 20 \n  --timeout 90
```

kyle: what's the ops manifest schema? we should be minimal: [{"op_name":"matmul","op_hash":"af3e9"},{...}] and an artifact-level fingerprint. that allows fast diffs.

zoe: exactly. linus earlier had an op-hash format we can reuse. we just need stable hashing across build steps.

maria: gating state machine suggestion: states = ingested -> delta-checks -> provisional | blocked -> full-bench-scheduled -> accepted | rejected. transitions reason-coded and auditable.

rahul: add a "provisional_accept_expires_at" field so console can surface TTL. if no bench completes, auto-fail after TTL.

devon: resource plan: delta-prober runs on cheaper worker type with fast priority; full bench uses high-memory GPU pool and lower priority. scheduler needs admission backpressure when full-bench queue > X.

kyle: quota policy: customers can purchase "accelerated full-bench slots" for faster turnaround; otherwise fall into deferred pool. keeps economics healthy.

maria: monitoring and alerts: 1) delta-prober false-positive rate (cases where provisional passed but full bench failed) 2) time-to-full-bench distribution 3) queue growth. we should aim FP rate < 1%.

zoe: privacy/attest: for private deployments we must ensure golden seeds don't leak. use family-local golden sets and optional customer-provided seeds. document that in onboarding.

rahul: security note: op-hash must be collision-resistant to avoid adversarial bypass. use sha256 over canonical op-descriptor. store only hashes in registry unless needed.

devon: follow-ups: - small RFC update capturing ops schema, delta-prober API, state machine, console signals, rollback automation - prototype delta-prober integration with scheduler - golden-set curation: who owns families?

kyle: I'll own golden-set ownership mapping and quota design.

maria: I'll draft the RFC update and include rollback runbooks.

zoe: I'll land the scheduler wiring for delta-prober prototype.

bench-bot: recent-run-summary: bench queue backlog peaked 3x last night; avg full-bench run = 47m; delta-prober target = 45-90s.

rahul: thanks. let's aim to have RFC PR + prototype in a week. ping #eng-ml for the review. :rocket:
